source: Grace Hill Demand Strategy 2H 2026 — The Play Book (WIP)
status: This describes a future state. The bundles are not launched and final contents are still being agreed. Read as the model being aligned on, not the model being run.
rules: No account enters a play without a recorded, dated reason to reach out. Not a segment. Not a persona match. A specific event or gap a person would recognize as a reason to make contact.
Never pitch the second bundle to the buyer who owns the first. Each bundle has its own budget owner — selling Resident & Prospect to an L&D leader asks them to spend a budget they don't control.

plays.name: Platform Core to Platform Plus
plays.note: The only play that reaches above the functions. Doubles as the fix for the largest loss reason — lack of executive support accounts for $759,717 across 36 lost deals, the biggest loss category by value.

plays.name: Market Data, Sold Standalone
plays.note: Do not lead with the platform. Blocking gap: there is no asset manager persona in the library — the budget owner for the fastest-growing product has never been documented. Build the persona before launching.

plays.name: Add Resident & Prospect Satisfaction
plays.note: 936 accounts. Runs on triggers and packaging, at scale.

plays.name: Core to Plus
plays.note: The easiest conversation we have. Workforce Excellence at Plus adds combo mystery shopping, which makes M3 a bridge into M1 — the shopping data becomes the evidence for the resident and prospect conversation.

plays.name: Land on Compliance, Designed to Expand
plays.note: The fastest land we have. Mid-market new logo converts at 36.1% against enterprise's 15.0%. The structural change: a new customer should exit into the cross-sell motion on close, with the gap already named.

plays.name: The First Cross-Sell
plays.note: 103 accounts with product data, all single-bundle. Do not launch before the commercial value proposition exists in usable form — a well-targeted list with the wrong message burns a 197-account segment too small to re-approach quickly.

plays.name: Re-Engagement
plays.note: 139 opportunities, $1.6M. Half of all lost revenue went to no decision rather than to a competitor. A competitive loss needs a better product or price; a no-decision loss needs presence until conditions change. Fastest play to start.

plays.name: Bundle Migration
plays.buyer: The current bundle owner, then the counterpart
plays.note: Three risks: customers feeling they now pay for capability they don't use; a discovery window that expires silently and reads as a takeaway; migration landing as a price conversation instead of an outcome conversation.

addOns.note: Add-ons attach to a bundle an account already holds. None is sold on its own, and the buyer is always whoever owns the bundle it attaches to.
addOns.realync: The only product in the portfolio going backward — revenue fell 7.7% last year. Buyers already get virtual leasing through platforms they own, so it loses a category evaluation on its own merits. The fix is distribution, not the product: attach it to Resident & Prospect Satisfaction where the marketing buyer is already ours, and lead with a conversion gap their own shopping or survey results already surfaced.
